Title: Yasin apologises, withdraws claims on drugs, money and influence in prisons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Composer and singer Yasin Sulaiman, 51, has publicly apologised to the Prisons Department and withdrawn controversial remarks he made in a recent podcast interview.
Yasin issued a video explanation on Instagram, along with a written statement expressing regret over his remarks of double standards and drug accessibility in prisons, which he said may have tarnished the reputation of the department.
"I, Yasin Sulaiman, take note of the explanation given by the Prisons Department regarding several matters I shared in recent podcasts and interviews about my experiences while in prison.
"I would like to explain that the sharing was based on what I experienced and understood during that period.
"At the time, before receiving treatment at Hospital Bahagia, I was experiencing an episode of bipolar mania. My condition at the time may have affected the way I saw, heard, understood and interpreted things happening around me," he said.
Yasin said he had never intended to tarnish the reputation of the department or belittle the duties of its officers and personnel through his podcast interviews.
"After taking note of the explanation by the Prisons Department and reflecting on the circumstances I went through at the time, I hereby withdraw the remarks.
"I regret if the sharing caused confusion or misunderstanding among the public.
"Therefore, I would like to apologise to the Prisons Department and its officers and personnel for the confusion caused," he said.
The singer, known for songs including Nur Kasih and Mimpi Laila, said he appreciated the work and service of the department's officers and personnel in carrying out their responsibilities.
"With this explanation, I hope any confusion arising from my previous sharing can be corrected and that this matter can be resolved amicably," he said.
Previously, Yasin was reported to have said that prison life was largely determined by money and influence, while drugs continued to enter prisons despite strict security checks on new inmates.
He described being made to strip and undergo repeated searches when he arrived at Sungai Buloh Prison, but said the measures had not stopped drugs from
circulating inside
.
The Prisons Department has since
denied the claims
.
Senior director of prison policy Mohamad Rosidek Musa said while some negative practices could occur, procedures were in place to prevent them.
In November 2023, the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Yasin of three drug-related charges but ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Perak.
On Sept 2, Yasin was allowed to return home as a free man after more than four years of legal proceedings and treatment for mental health issues, after he was certified as having recovered and being in a stable condition.

Title: NST Leader: Help workers go where the jobs are
Article:
As the Malaysian economy climbs the value chain, nothing matters more than a labour force that is welltrained, agile, and above all, highly mobile across the country.
This is why the news that the government will provide a one-off RM1,000 MobilityAssistance allowance to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors who take up jobs more than 100km away from home is so welcome.
It is a right step towards making the employment safety net more responsive to today's labour market. The basic premise is sound: go where the job is.
Distance, relocation, transport, new accommodation and other up-front costs ought not to be such prohibitive hindrances as to discourage the matching of job opportunities with job seekers. This allowance is not a stand-alone idea.
Greater improvements have gone into the Employment Insurance Scheme, such as raising the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 to 50 per cent of the remaining Job Search Allowance, the daily training allowance to RM30 and the maximum training fee to RM7,000.
There is always roomto do better for our workers. Review the RM1,000 allowance regularly rather than wait until costs rise significantly. Consider distance and regional variables.
A flat RM1,000 allowance is a different value proposition depending on whether a job-seeker moves 100km within a state or relocates across the South China Sea.
Even moving within Sarawak can involve a distance of 1,000km over difficult terrain. Simplify application procedures. The allowance ismeant to ease taking out-of-townjobs, and an overly cumbersome process may negate it.
The Malaysian Employers Federation has stressed accessibility, awareness and timely pay-out. Ideally, eligibility, documentation and pay-out timelines are clearly communicated and handled digitally. Link job-mobility assistancemore closely to job-matching.
Perkeso already provides employment services and matches unemployed contributors with vacancies throughMYFutureJobs. The allowance could be devised more strategically to encourage job-seekers to consider suitable vacancies beyond their immediate vicinity.
Monitor and measure the allowance's efficacy. Perkeso should publish data on takeup rates, types of jobs secured, destinations and whether recipients actually remain employed.
The allowance must not become a one-off incentive. It needs to be dynamic, reflecting an ever-changing employment scene and the evolving needs of our workers.
The booming data-centre industry and the advent of artificial intelligence will greatly affect the Malaysian job market in coming years.
Perkeso and the Human Resources Ministry will do well to assess where jobs will appear (and disappear), and ensure workers are not just well-trained and able to adjust but flexible enough to go where new jobs may proliferate.
Employees and employers alike must strive to stay ahead of the curve as the economy transforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5-year-old girl's prayer request becomes family's final memory
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A simple request from 5-year-old Putri Nur Afiyah Qalesya Mustafa to join her for Isyak prayers last night became the family's final memory of her before she was found dead in Kampung Padang today.
Her grandmother, Mahani Mad Som, 63, said she found it unusual when the girl asked her father to pray with her for the first time.
"Yesterday, she seemed different from usual. She asked for instant noodles with a runny-yolk egg, then asked her father to pray with her. It was the first time she had ever asked him to pray with her.
"My granddaughter was a bright little girl. She always picked things up quickly whenever we taught her something," she said when met at her home today.
Mahani said she realised her granddaughter was missing at about 9am after breakfast, when she found the girl's cradle empty and immediately alerted the child's father.
"I had a bad feeling when I called out to her by the cradle, and she did not respond. We immediately started looking for her and found her lying face down in the river. Her father rushed in and pulled her out," she said.
The river is about 300 metres from the family home and can be reached via an unpaved path through an orchard.
Mahani said children in the village would not go to the river alone as they had to pass through the orchard to get there.
She said her son, who was detained by police to assist investigations into her granddaughter's death, had previously received treatment for mental health problems at Permai Hospital in Tampoi.
He was also scheduled to collect his medication at Kota Tinggi Hospital this morning.
Police arrested the 37-year-old uncle this morning on suspicion of throwing the child into the river, resulting in her death.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the suspect was detained after police received a report at 9.30am that he had gone on a rampage while armed with a parang.
He said police were still investigating the motive and circumstances of the incident under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.

Title: Erosion of Germany's political centre exposes Merz's weakening grip on power
Article:
GERMANY'S far right and far left both made big gains in Sunday's state elections, exposing yet again the erosion of the political centre in Europe's largest economy as well as Chancellor Friedrich Merz's weakening hold on power.
The anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) confirmed its strength in the formerly communist eastern states by taking first place in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state, building on its triumph two weeks ago in Saxony-Anhalt.
The AfD also recorded its best-ever result in Berlin, where the far-left Left Party came first and looks set to replace Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) in the mayor's office.
Merz called the result in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania  — the worst in CDU history — "a disaster."
But he defied speculation he might step down, pledging to remain to pass a package of tax and pension reforms that he hopes will help revive Germany's sluggish economy.
For now, at least, the party has stood behind him, although the result will add to pressure within his coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD), some of whom want to water down parts of the reform agenda.
"We have to analyse, as a government, why there is this sense of uncertainty in the country," SPD co-leader Lars Klingbeil said.
A pervasive sense of economic malaise and disillusion with traditional political parties point to further turbulence ahead, with a raft of state elections in western Germany due next year.
"Germany is entering a period of political instability where viable coalitions are harder and harder to build, and that doesn't bode well for Europe when Germany is the de facto leader," said Sudha David-Wilp, a senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the United States.
The AfD wants to expel foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, while the Left Party wants to cap rents and nationalise large parts of the Berlin housing market.
By contrast, Merz's pursuit of what he says are painful but necessary reforms has yet to yield improvements that voters can feel.
"We can see how difficult it is to win people over while in government and from the centre of society," said Stefan Evers, the CDU's lead candidate in Berlin.
Even before the election, Merz's approval ratings were at a record low and his party has trailed the AfD in national polling for months.
"People would tell us that as long as he had a say in things, we wouldn't vote for you," said one CDU election campaigner in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
From the start of his time in office, when a normally routine parliamentary vote to confirm him as chancellor turned into a humiliation requiring a second round of voting, Merz has struggled to establish his authority.
[[nid:1537874]]
There have been repeated gaffes, from saying people in Germany needed to work longer hours to identifying as "middle class" while working as a highly remunerated board member of BlackRock Asset Management.
Surveys indicate that his communication lapses and his difficulty in establishing an emotional connection with voters anxious about their economic future both contributed to the outcome of all five state elections this year.
But Germany's deep-seated economic challenges —  an ageing population, poor growth and the erosion of its industrial base under increasing pressure from China — resist easy solutions.
The reforms themselves caused problems in formerly communist eastern Germany, where despite more than three decades of economic transformation, more voters than in the west earn the minimum wage and rely completely on the state pension in retirement.
Manuela Schwesig, the SPD state premier of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, whose success in limiting the AfD's gains in her state was one of the few bright spots for the government, said she was "surprised" by Merz's refusal to change course.
Her campaign was heavily critical of Merz, whom she accused of showing indifference towards voters struggling with soaring fuel prices.
She also called for changes to the pension reform that would require people to work for longer — a particularly unpopular issue in the east, where many have not built up the same level of savings as those in the west.
Days before the vote, as speculation grew that his position might be in danger, senior CDU leaders rallied around the chancellor, aware that replacing him would put the reform programme at risk without solving underlying problems.
So far, the policy — known as the 'firewall' — under which the mainstream parties refuse to cooperate with the AfD has kept it from sharing power.
But there are growing doubts about whether it is possible to exclude a party which enjoys the support of more voters in Germany than any other.
Despite reservations about cooperating with a party with elements that are classified by the domestic security services as extremist right-wing, there are growing calls in the CDU for a rethink.
"This 'firewall' hasn't done anything for the CDU and they need to think about that," said Leif-Erik Holm, the AfD's lead candidate in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
Opinion polls have shown deep disillusion among many voters with a political system that has seen a succession of coalitions between the formerly fiercely antagonistic mainstream parties of the centre-right and centre-left.
Under former Chancellor Angela Merkel, the "grand coalition" of CDU and SPD, seen only once before at federal level during the 1960s, became standard.
Merz, once seen as a firebrand conservative, repeated the exercise after another coalition, headed by SPD Chancellor Olaf Scholz, collapsed in 2024.
"It's just allowed a vacuum on the right and the left for these parties to emerge," David-Wilp said.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Rauf leaves three messages for civil servants ahead of Melaka assembly dissolution
Article:
AYER KEROH: With the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly expected to be announced tomorrow, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has left three key messages to ensure continuity in the state's development efforts.
The three messages are to uphold integrity, use artificial intelligence (AI) wisely and make the Melaka Sayang Rakyat (MeSRa) agenda the heart of public service.
He said positions held by civil servants were not a privilege but a trust that must be carried out responsibly to maintain public confidence in the civil service.
"Do not let one wrong decision tarnish your own name and cause the people's trust in the entire civil service to be affected.
"If we hold the people's trust, we must never trade it away," he said in his speech at the Melaka State Public Service Workers Appreciation Night.
Also present were state legislative assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum, state secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh and senior state executive councillor Datuk Rais Yasin.
Rauf said civil servants must also be prepared to embrace technological developments by using AI to improve the efficiency of service delivery to the people.
"I want Melaka civil servants to use AI to work faster, more accurately and better.
"But remember, use AI to help us think, not to replace our thinking," he said.
For his third message, he urged all civil servants to make MeSRa the heart of their responsibilities and service to the community.
He said the effectiveness of a government should not be measured solely by the slogans or policies it promotes, but by people's experience when dealing with the government and how effectively their problems were resolved.
"Because ultimately, the people do not judge the government by the slogans we proclaim, but by the treatment they receive and the problems we solve," he said.
Rauf said the spirit of togetherness among civil servants must be maintained to ensure the state administration continued to function effectively in the people's interest.
He said if he was entrusted to continue leading the state administration, he hoped the spirit of togetherness would be preserved.
"We will continue what is good, improve what is lacking and, most importantly, ensure the state administration continues to move forward for the people and for Melaka," he said.
He also expressed his appreciation to all civil servants who played a key role in ensuring the state government's agendas and programmes were implemented.
They included staff from the Management Services Division of the Melaka Chief Minister's Department, Tourism Promotion Division of the State Communications, Multimedia and Tourism Committee, Technical and Logistics Division, as well as members of the media in Melaka.
"My media friends, I know they are the hardest to admit when they are tired. Not only do they have to rush to my programmes from morning until night, but wherever I go now, whenever there is a press conference, there is always one question being asked: Datuk Seri, when are you dissolving the state assembly?
"I go to a programme, they ask. I visit a village, they ask again. Even if they see me walking a little faster, they might think I am on my way to announce the dissolution! Just be patient until the time comes. I will know what to do," he said.

Title: Wira driver in viral NSE incident remanded two days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The driver of a Proton Wira linked to a viral incident that saw a Perodua Axia crash into a ditch along the North-South Expressway has been remanded for two days.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said the man was arrested at his home in Puchong early today.
"We have also obtained a two-day remand order against the driver to facilitate further investigations," he said when contacted today.
The arrest comes after police
said yesterday that they were tracking down the Wira driver following the incident between KM270 and KM275 of the North-South Expressway.
Two dashcam recordings of the incident have since gone viral on social media.
The footage shows the Proton Wira moving into the lane occupied by the Perodua Axia, prompting the Axia driver to take evasive action.
The Axia subsequently loses control, veers off the expressway and ends up in a ditch.
Hasbullah had earlier urged anyone with information on the Wira or its driver to come forward to assist investigations.
He also advised motorists to drive cautiously and exercise patience and consideration towards other road users.
Hasbullah said the widespread use of dashcams meant incidents on the road could be captured on video, with such footage potentially assisting police investigations and appropriate action being taken in accordance with the law.

Title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strongly condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, while reaffirming its solidarity with the Kingdom.
The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia's efforts to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the safety of its population, in line with the United Nations Charter and international law.
"Malaysia also supports all efforts towards de-escalation and an immediate end to the hostilities," it said in a statement today.
The statement follows an escalation in regional hostilities, with Saudi authorities confirming that a ballistic missile fired towards Riyadh on Sept 19 was intercepted and destroyed.
Saudi Gazette reported that the Houthis also attempted to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in Baish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu, but the attacks were thwarted.
The Saudi Press Agency reported that Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif on Sept 14 injured 13 civilians and damaged several houses and vehicles, according to the Saudi-led coalition.
The Foreign Ministry reaffirmed the importance of Malaysia's longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.
"Malaysia attaches great importance to its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia, and remains fully committed to further strengthening this partnership for mutual interests of both nations," the ministry said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: eKYC providers update systems for new-generation MyKad
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) service providers are updating their systems to recognise the design and features of the new-generation MyKad during identity verification.
The National Registration Department (NRD), in a statement, said the move followed difficulties faced by some new-generation MyKad holders when undergoing identity verification through eKYC systems.
Several engagement sessions have been and are being held with relevant agencies and eKYC service providers to address the issue and ensure identity verification processes run smoothly.
"NRD has provided the necessary information and is monitoring the implementation of the updates to expedite the system adaptation process," it said.
Pending completion of the updates, NRD advised users experiencing difficulties with eKYC verification using the new-generation MyKad to contact their respective institutions or service providers for information on available alternative verification methods.
NRD said the new-generation MyKad, officially issued from Sept 17, featured improvements in its structure, design, technology and security features to enhance identity protection.
"The adaptation of eKYC systems by service providers is part of the transition process to support the use of the new card," it said.
The department said it would continue monitoring the system update process and work with relevant agencies and service providers until the adaptation was completed.
"NRD's priority is to ensure the transition to the new-generation MyKad is carried out in an orderly manner without affecting public convenience in accessing services that require identity verification," it said.
Agencies and eKYC service providers requiring further information or clarification on the features of the new-generation MyKad can contact NRD via email at commandset@jpn.gov.my

Title: MoE scraps 30pc Bumiputera equity requirement for private institutions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The education ministry has scrapped the requirement for private education institutions to maintain at least 30 per cent Bumiputera equity ownership.
In a statement, it said the decision was reached following discussions with the investment, trade and industry ministry.
It said the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity threshold for institutions operating through Sdn Bhd companies, as set out in the Private Education Institution Policy Statement Book published in 2006, would no longer apply as a condition.
The ministry said the adjustment was made to meet the current needs of the education sector and ensure participation in education remained open to all parties wishing to contribute to the nation's educational development.
It added that it valued the contributions of all private education institution operators and would continue working with stakeholders in the interest of education.
Yesterday, the ministry said it would propose
a review of tuition centre ownership
rules to the cabinet next week following concerns over a proposed 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement.
On Saturday, MIC National Strategic Director Datuk C. Sivaraj called on the ministry to clarify the proposed equity requirement.
Sivaraj said efforts to increase Bumiputera participation in the economy should not come at the expense of the rights and equity of non-Bumiputera communities through licensing conditions, rulings or administrative regulations.

Title: E-hailing, p-hailing demand expected to surge up to 300pct during F1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Demand for e-hailing and p-hailing services is expected to surge by 200 to 300 per cent in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) scheduled for October.
Pertubuhan Lestari Ekonomi Aktivis Digital Malaysia (Lead Malaysia) said in a statement that the projection was based on typical demand patterns seen during large-scale international events.
It said the spike in demand was expected to be concentrated around Sepang, Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Putrajaya, creating opportunities for thousands of gig drivers and riders to boost their income during the period.
"We also anticipate dynamic fare increases at specific times and locations when demand exceeds driver availability following the influx of F1 fans from around the world.
"We are confident many drivers from neighbouring states will travel to the Klang Valley and Sepang to seize earning opportunities during the event.
"For delivery riders, the increased visitor numbers will also boost demand for food and parcel delivery in key areas," Lead Malaysia said.
Lead Malaysia also reminded e-hailing and p-hailing drivers that as they pursue bookings, bonuses, incentives and dynamic fares, they also represent the nation.
"During race week, every trip is not just a booking. It is also a small opportunity to introduce Malaysia to the world.
"Lead Malaysia is confident that our drivers and delivery riders will always prioritise guests and customers, maintaining courtesy, politeness and professionalism," it said.
Malaysia will be hosting the Bahrain GP from Oct 2 to 4 following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement allows the Bahrain GP to remain on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier in the season due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

Title: Trip to collect medicine ends in tragedy for 5-year-old girl
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The 5-year-old girl who died after allegedly being thrown into a river in Kampung Padang here today had returned to Tanjung Sedili with her father to collect medication before the tragedy.
Sedili assemblyman Muszaidi Makmor said the victim had returned with her 40-year-old father, who lives and runs a food business in Muar.
"The suspect also returned to Tanjung Sedili with them. Regrettably, the suspect, who is believed to be mentally unstable, acted unpredictably," Muszaidi shared in a Facebook post today.
Muszaidi, who visited the girl's father at the Tanjung Sedili Health Clinic this afternoon, expressed his condolences to the family and prayed for their strength.
Earlier, police reported that a 37-year-old local man had been arrested after allegedly
throwing his 5-year-old niece
into a river, resulting in her death.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the suspect was arrested after police received a report about the incident at 9.30am.
He said the suspect allegedly threw the girl into the river before going on a rampage armed with a parang and chasing the victim's father.

Title: Four goats killed, 20 rescued in barn fire
Article:
BALING: Four goats were burnt to death while 20 others were saved by villagers after a livestock barn caught fire in Kampung Baru Bakai, Kuala Ketil, today.
Baling Fire and Rescue Station chief Assistant Fire Superintendent Zulkhairi Mat Tanjil said the department received an emergency call regarding the barn fire at 3.35pm.
"A team from the Baling station, led by Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Najmi Ismail, arrived at the scene and found the barn ablaze.
"A Proton Gen 2 was 95 per cent destroyed, while a lorry sustained five per cent damage in the fire," he said when contacted today.
Zulkhairi said firefighters managed to control the blaze at 4.20pm and extinguished it fully by 4.49pm.
He added that the cause of the fire and total losses are still under investigation, with no human casualties or injuries reported.

Title: MAHB reminds road users to observe traffic rules near KKIA
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) has reminded road users to observe traffic regulations and practise responsible road sharing following a video showing cyclists on the access road to Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA).
The video shows several cyclists riding along the airport access road, alongside other motorists.
MAHB said it was aware of the video circulating on social media.
"While the access road remains open and accessible to public traffic, we strongly emphasise that safety is our utmost priority.
"We kindly remind and urge all road users, including motorists, motorcyclists and cyclists, to exercise vigilance, observe traffic regulations and practise responsible road sharing," it said in a statement.

Title: Frontken unit buys industrial land, factory buildings in Taiwan for RM118mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Frontken Corporation Bhd's subsidiary, Ares Green Technology Corporation, is acquiring industrial land and the factory buildings erected thereon in Tainan City, Taiwan, from Ginwin Technology Co Ltd for RM118.16 million.
Ginwin Technology is a 53.45 per cent-owned subsidiary of Taiwan-based company, Enlight Corporation.
Frontken said the property is currently utilised as a thin-film-transistor liquid-crystal display colour filter recycling facility. The property is 16,172 sq m of industrial land with seven existing factory buildings.
"The acquisition is expected to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
Frontken said Ares Green currently anticipates commencing the first phase of the construction of new production lines in the first half of 2027 with an estimated investment of approximately NT$620 million (RM79.6 million).
"The first phase of the construction is expected to take approximately one to 1.5 years, and Ares Green intends to implement the subsequent phases progressively, taking into consideration its business requirements and customer demand," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ranhill shares jump 8pct to all-time high
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ranhill Utilities Bhd's shares hit an all time high on Monday, lifted by rising demand for industrial water infrastructure and Johor's data centre boom.
The counter rose 8.25 per cent or 24 sen on Monday to close at RM3.15 versus Friday's closing price of RM2.91.
The stock saw more than three million shares traded throughout the day.
Ranhill's share price has risen 86.39 per cent on a year-to-date basis and it is currently valued at RM3.77 billion.
In a note dated Sept 18, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd said Ranhill is poised to benefit from the restructuring of Johor's water sector on the back of the state's tariff hike and the rise in data centre demand.
HLIB said the August 2025 rise in tariff had materially strengthened Ranhill SAJ Sdn Bhd's earnings outlook.
For the financial year ended June 30, 2026, Ranhill posted a net profit of RM196.61 million while its revenue stood at RM2.49 billion.

Title: Markets brace for tighter Fed path: CIMB Securities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Financial markets are pricing a more hawkish US Federal Reserve interest rate path than the latest forecasts from policymakers and economists:
This could keep the US dollar supported into 2027, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The firm said markets are pricing about 80 basis points of additional Fed tightening in 2027, equivalent to roughly 3.2 rate hikes.
This is in comparison with the latest Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) projections for a 25-basis-point increase in the fourth quarter of 2026 and no further hikes in 2027.
The FOMC's latest projection puts the policy rate at 4.25 per cent after the expected fourth-quarter move.
CIMB Securities said market forecasts for end-2027 rates remain widely dispersed, ranging from 3.25 per cent to 4.50 per cent, with a median of 3.50 per cent.
The firm said near-term upside risks to global energy prices and potential price shocks could keep markets positioned for tighter US monetary policy in the fourth quarter of 2026.
It also revised higher its forecasts for US Treasury yields relative to German and Japanese government bonds.
CIMB Securities raised its end-2027 two-year US Treasury-Bund and US Treasury-JGB spread assumptions by eight basis points and 15 basis points to about 160 basis points and 270 basis points respectively.
The wider yield advantage is expected to support the dollar and reduce the case for sustained appreciation in the euro and yen.
CIMB Securities said a return of Brent crude to US$100 a barrel could provide another source of support for the dollar, particularly as higher energy prices tend to weigh on currencies of major energy importers.
The firm retained its near-term US Dollar Index (DXY) forecast at 101 but raised the third-quarter 2027 projection to 100.
However, a decline in Brent below US$90 a barrel could reduce that support, with the DXY ceiling estimated at 99.8 under a lower oil-price scenario.
For Asian currencies, CIMB Securities said the impact of higher US rates could be partly offset by relatively stable Chinese yuan conditions and higher regional yields.
It expects Asian currencies to remain within their 12-month forecast ranges, with potential yuan strength ahead of a China-US summit providing some stability for the ringgit, Singapore dollar and Thai baht.
Higher oil prices and US rates pose greater near-term risks to the Indonesian rupiah, they said, potentially adding pressure for a 25-basis-point Bank Indonesia rate hike in the fourth quarter of 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5-year-old girl dies after allegedly thrown into river by uncle
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Police have arrested a 37-year-old man on suspicion of throwing his 5-year-old niece into a river, causing her death, in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili, today.
District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the suspect was arrested after police received a report on the incident at about 9.30am.
He said the suspect allegedly threw the victim into the river before going on a rampage armed with a parang and chasing a 40-year-old man.
"Acting on information, a team from the Kuala Sedili police station went to the scene and arrested the suspect.
"A struggle ensued during the arrest, resulting in an injury to a police officer, but the suspect was successfully apprehended," he said in a statement today.
Yusof said an assistant medical officer who arrived at the scene confirmed the child's death.

Title: Bursa Malaysia stays up on bargain hunting of blue chips
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended slightly higher on Monday, supported by bargain hunting in selected blue chips as concerns over the West Asia conflict eased amid retreating oil prices.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.38 points, or 0.08 per cent, to 1,666.94, from Friday's close of 1,665.56.
The benchmark index opened 1.36 points lower at 1,664.20 and moved between 1,661.22 and 1,674.74 throughout the session.
Market breadth was positive, with gainers outpacing decliners 654 to 552. A total of 517 counters were unchanged, 1,159 untraded and 20 suspended.
Turnover narrowed to 3.41 billion units worth RM2.8 billion, from 4.91 billion units valued at RM4.87 billion on Friday.
Berjaya Research Sdn Bhd head of research Kenneth Leong said he expects the FBM KLCI to seek stability, with any further gains likely to remain measured amid persistent external uncertainties, particularly elevated US bond yields, ongoing West Asia tensions and expectations of further US Federal Reserve tightening. "Investors are likely to remain selective, with the index potentially consolidating in the near term while awaiting fresh domestic and global catalysts," he told Bernama.
From a technical perspective, Leong said the key index has formed a bullish "candlestick" pattern, although it could potentially enter a consolidation phase. "The immediate resistance levels remain at 1,687 points, followed by 1,700 points, while the supports are now at 1,655 points and 1,650 points," he added.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the recent correction could encourage selective bargain hunting. However, the lack of fresh domestic catalysts and continued concerns over elevated US Treasury yields are likely to limit the sustainability of any near-term recovery.
"Recent trading has also shown investors shifting some attention away from index heavyweights towards smaller-cap opportunities, while sentiment towards the broader market remains mixed.
"Looking ahead, we expect the FBM KLCI to remain in consolidation mode this week in the absence of a fresh catalyst," he added.
Thong said investors are likely to remain selective while monitoring developments surrounding the US-China summit, movements in crude oil prices and US Treasury yields.
Among the heavyweight counters, Malayan Banking Bhd rose six sen to RM10.38, while Public Bank Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhd both added two sen each to RM4.79 and RM7.65, respectively.
Tenaga Nasional Bhd remained unchanged at RM13.04, and IHH Healthcare Bhd eased one sen to RM7.63.
As for the most active counters, Zetrix AI Bhd and AirAsia Group Bhd were both flat at 20 sen and 53 sen, respectively.
Jaks Resources Bhd gained 1.5 sen to 17 sen, FSBM Holdings Bhd added three sen to 9.5 sen and HHRG Bhd dipped half a sen to 16.5 sen.
Among the top gainers, Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd recovered RM1 to RM4.34, Samaiden Group Bhd expanded 43 sen to RM2.38, and Hong Leong Bank Bhd bounced 38 sen to RM22.92.
Solarvest Holdings Bhd rallied 36 sen to RM3.69, and Petron Malaysia Refining and Marketing Bhd jumped 33 sen to RM3.79.
Of the top losers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd erased 86 sen to RM41.94, Time Dotcom Bhd dropped 47 sen to RM5.94, and Sunway Construction Bhd tumbled 42 sen to RM7.46.
QL Resources Bhd lost 24 sen to RM3.95, and Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd was 22 sen lower to RM7.58.

Title: Anwar conveys condolences on passing of former deputy minister Yahya Lampong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former rural development deputy minister Datuk Yahya Lampong, who passed away today.
Yahya, who was also a former member of parliament for Kota Belud, died at a hospital here at 6am. He was 86.
In a Facebook post, Anwar expressed his sadness upon receiving news of Yahya's passing.
"My deepest condolences to the family of the deceased. May Allah SWT forgive all his sins, accept his good deeds, and place him among the believers. Al-Fatihah," he said.
Yahya served as MP for Kota Belud from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 general election.
He also served as the state assemblyman for Tempasuk under the United Sabah National Organisation (USNO) banner from 1985 to 1986.
His political career began in 1981 when he contested the Usukan state seat representing Berjaya.

Title: Govt working to expedite claims for victims of FDS helicopter crash – Dzulkefly
Article:
TAIPING: The Health Ministry is working with the Public Service Department's Pension Division and the Finance Ministry to expedite benefits for the families of victims of the Sept 8 flying doctor service helicopter crash in Sarawak.
The benefits include death ex-gratia payments, retirement benefits and other claims.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measure was underway to ensure the victims' next of kin receive the support and benefits they are entitled to.
"I cannot state the details, but the calculations include everything in great detail, and they are currently computing all of that. The ex-gratia has many components to it," he told reporters after conducting a working visit to the Taiping Hospital here today.
The crash on Sept 8 claimed the lives of all five individuals on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3.40 pm.
The victims who perished were medical officer Dr. Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31, two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44, as well as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30.
Dzulkefly added that the ministry has not set a specific timeframe for the temporary suspension of FDS operations.
He said operations would only resume after the authorities complete their official investigation findings.
"As soon as we can restart, we will restart. We won't wait. But until a decision is made, everything depends on the investigation outcome and so forth.
"So, we will wait for the investigation outcome, and immediately after that, we will take steps to make decisions regarding subsequent services," he said.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the health ministry has allocated over RM1.65 million to upgrade and improve facilities at Taiping Hospital adding that the allocation involves upgrading, renovation, and repair works covering healthcare facilities, restrooms, and other areas.
He said this amount is an increase compared to the allocation of RM571,000 last year for improvement works involving the hospital's Emergency Department and psychiatric ward, which has already been fully completed.

Title: Dialog secures US$81mil Raja cluster nod from Petronas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd has secured final investment decision (FID) approval from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) for an US$81 million cluster development and abandonment plan.
The approval covers the development and eventual abandonment of the Raja cluster small field asset under a production sharing contract (PSC).
The PSC was signed between Petronas, through Malaysia Petroleum Management, and Dialog Resources Sdn Bhd on Dec 5, 2024.
The contract has a tenure of up to 14 years, comprising a two-year pre-development phase, a two-year development phase and a 10-year production phase, or until the contract expires, whichever is earlier.
First commercial production is expected by the end of the two-year development phase.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Dialog said the pre-development phase included 3D seismic data reprocessing, specialised studies and resource assessments to support development planning.
The development will utilise Dialog's Tarpon platform system which is designed for marginal field developments in water depths of less than 100 metres.
Dialog currently operates the Baram junior cluster small field assets PSC.
The Raja PSC is expected to further strengthen its operational expertise while creating synergies by allowing the group to leverage its integrated technical services team.
Funding for the contract will be internally generated or through external borrowings.
Dialog's share price closed 3.83 per cent or eight sen lower on Monday at RM2.01, valuing the company at RM11.35 billion.

Title: Powerwell bags record RM190.4mil data centre orders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Powerwell Holdings Bhd has secured two purchase orders worth a combined RM190.4 million to supply low-voltage switchgear and related equipment for a data centre project in Johor.
Its wholly-owned subsidiary Powerwell International Sdn Bhd received the orders from a returning customer, with the contracts expected to contribute to the company's financial performance from the current financial year ending March 31, 2027 (FY27) through FY28.
Powerwell said the combined award is the largest in its history.
The orders will also lift the group's order book, which stood at RM268.9 million as of end-June 2026, excluding the latest contracts.
The company said demand for power distribution equipment continues to be supported by data centre development, while its tender pipeline includes projects spanning data centres, renewable energy, semiconductors and infrastructure.
The latest contracts come as Powerwell expands its manufacturing capacity to cater to demand.
The company said the orders from a returning customer also reflect its ability to handle large-scale requirements and support longer-term customer relationships.
Powerwell, which manufactures low- and medium-voltage electrical distribution equipment, said it is continuing to broaden its product and manufacturing capabilities while monitoring market and macroeconomic conditions.
The company said the latest wins follow a record financial performance in FY26 and a positive start to FY27.
The group's manufacturing expansion is expected to support its ability to undertake larger orders as demand from data centres and other power-intensive industries grows.
Powerwell did not disclose the identity or value of the individual data centre project beyond the combined RM190.4 million purchase orders.
The latest award brings additional visibility to the group's earnings through FY28, against a backdrop of continued investment in digital infrastructure and other industrial projects.

Title: 'H' series sets RTD record with RM91.2mil haul, taxi drivers to benefit – Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Special registration number H1 fetched a record RM10.78 million, leading a fiercely contested 'H' series bidding exercise that attracted more than 34,000 bidders.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the five-day bidding exercise through the JPJeBid system, which began on Sept 16, saw 8,223 registration numbers successfully bid for out of 34,664 participants.
The bidding generated RM91,206,642 in total, comprising RM89,266,542 from successful bids and RM1,940,100 in service fees.
"H1 stole the spotlight with the highest bid of RM10,777,777, followed by H9 at RM4,969,999 and H3 at RM4,209,777.
"H5 recorded a bid of RM4,007,777, H8 RM4 million and H6 RM3.38 million," he said in a statement today.
Loke said other numbers among the highest bids were H2 at RM3.18 million, H7 (RM3.1 million), H4 (RM2,437,777) and H11 (RM1,557,777).
He said H1001 and H100 attracted the highest number of bidders, with 37 each.
H1805 received 36 bidders, while H1777 and H4818 attracted 32 bidders each.
Loke said the success of the H series special registration numbers reflected not only strong demand for special registration numbers but also the government's digital transformation through the JPJeBid platform.
"The platform has made the bidding process easier, faster, more efficient and transparent," he said.
He said revenue generated through the initiative would be channeled back to the people through various programmes and initiatives by the Transport Ministry and Road Transport Department, including road safety programmes and initiatives that directly benefit the public.
"Therefore, the success of the H series NPI is not merely about figures or registration numbers, but carries greater value for the people and the country," he said.
Loke said the government would continue to accelerate the digitalisation of public services and introduce high-impact initiatives to improve delivery efficiency.
He said these efforts were also aimed at ensuring national revenue was translated into benefits that could be felt by the people.
In a Facebook post, Loke added that the H series was linked to taxi registration numbers, and proceeds from the bidding would be used to assist taxi and rental car drivers nationwide.
"H was originally a registration number series for taxis.

The H1 registration number attracted attention earlier after its
RM10.7 million bid value
went viral on social media following the end of bidding for the special H series yesterday.
The H series was open for bidding through the JPJeBid system from Sept 16 to 20, involving numbers H1 to H9999.
The special registration number series was launched by RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli on Sept 14 in conjunction with
Malaysia Day celebrations.

Title: European Union fines Google US$462mil for data location breach
Article:
DUBLIN: Ireland's data protection watchdog, acting on behalf of the European Union, said Monday that it had fined Google 403 million euros (US$462 million) for improperly using users' location data.
The technology giant infringed the EU's General Data Protection Regulation between May 2018 and February 2020, Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC), which is charged with applying the bloc's rules over the issue, said in a statement.
In its final decision after opening an inquiry in February 2020, the DPC ruled that Google infringed the GDPR "in respect of the lawfulness and fairness of its processing of location data in web and app activity and location history."
DPC deputy commissioner Graham Doyle said that "as a result of Google's failures... individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests."
He added that "the retention of users' location data for longer than necessary aggravated this loss of control."
Alongside the fine, the regulator said it had "ordered Google to bring its processing into compliance within six months."
In response, Google said the "case centres around historical policies that have since been updated."
"From 2019 onwards, we've significantly evolved our practices and launched robust tools that make managing location data simple," the company added in a statement.--AFP

Title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico to sue Trump administration over White House access
Article:

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar leaves Istana Hinggap after nearly an hour
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim left Istana Hinggap Negri Sembilan in Bukit Persekutuan here after an audience lasting nearly an hour with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
His vehicle was part of a convoy accompanied by police motorcycle escorts that departed at 6.57pm.
Anwar sought an audience with Tuanku Muhriz amid heightened tensions surrounding the adat and constitutional crisis enveloping the state.
Members of the media had gathered outside the palace from 2pm ahead of the expected meeting.
On Friday, Anwar stressed the need for the Negri Sembilan government to adhere strictly to constitutional provisions and established procedures in resolving the dispute over the throne.
He said the removal of a ruler was not a trivial matter and that any action involving the monarchy
must comply fully
with the Constitution.
The dispute stems from an April 19 proclamation by four people claiming to be Undang Yang Empat, the territorial chiefs whose votes determine the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, announcing Tuanku Muhriz's removal under Article 10(1)(b) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959.
They also subsequently proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
However, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang, which governs the Undang institution, ruled on Sept 14 that the proclamation was unconstitutional and invalid.
The Negri Sembilan exco members then issued a statement on Sept 16 affirming that Tuanku Muhriz's removal in April was legitimate and Tuanku Nadzaruddin was the new ruler.
The following day, Ismail endorsed the statement and called for its official gazettement.
But later the same day, the
Attorney-General's Chambers
said the proclamation was invalid as it did not meet the mandatory requirements of Article 10, including the absence of evidence that any grounds for disqualification applied to Tuanku Muhriz.
It said Article 10 prescribed the procedures and grounds that had to be satisfied before such action could be taken.
On Sunday, Tuanku Muhriz r
evoked the appointments
of all 10 exco members with immediate effect, citing breach of their oath of office.
Ismail has since
disputed the move,
saying any action to dismiss or terminate an exco member without the menteri besar's advice or request would be a legal error, unconstitutional and have no legal effect.
He said he had never been consulted or advised on the termination of any exco member.

Title: Malaysia’s ‘elephant whisperer’ leads push to save Sabah’s endangered Bornean elephants
Article:
SUKAU, Sept 21 — Deep in Malaysia’s Borneo jungle, wild shouts fill the air as a Bornean elephant is darted and her angry herd rallies to protect her.
The downed elephant is one of only around 1,000 Bornean elephants left in the wild, and the team that darted her is working to protect the endangered species by minimising growing conflict between the animals and local communities.
Once the herd has been chased off, conservationist Farina Othman and her team move in to attach a tracking collar to the animal.
This photo taken on August 24, 2026, shows Farina measuring the length of a female Bornean elephant’s leg during a GPS collaring operation as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
The collar allows them to alert villagers if the elephant strays too near.
It is also key to a programme Farina is designing to create “corridors” for elephants roaming a fragmented landscape of virgin forest patches, hemmed in by vast oil palm plantations and villages.
Farina has studied these elephants for years, earning her the nickname “Borneo’s elephant whisperer” as well as the prestigious Whitley Award for conservationists.
This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a wild female Bornean elephant with a GPS collar around her neck crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
“It’s Pigtail,” she whispered, stroking the tranquilised elephant’s trunk and nodding to the distinctive tail that prompted its nickname.
The team works fast — the dart’s sedative effects last only half an hour, and the herd can still be heard nearby. Overhead, there are flashes of lightning as a tropical thunderstorm approaches.
As soon as the collar is securely fastened and blood samples are taken, the team, accompanied by AFP journalists, retreat into the forest before Pigtail rouses.
‘Conflict inevitable’
This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a herd of wild Bornean elephants crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
For the past 40 years, Bornean elephants have lost more than 60 per cent of their habitat in Sabah, in northern Borneo, to logging and, later, oil palm expansion, according to the International Union for Conservation of Nature, which listed the animal as endangered in 2024.
Lower Kinabatangan, a floodplain in eastern Sabah of around 400 square kilometres, is home to around 160 elephants.
But “only half of that is now a space left for the elephants,” said Farina, a Malaysian academic who heads local conservation group Seratu Aatai, or “Solidarity” in the local Sungai language.
When the animals venture into private property or nearby villages, “conflict is inevitable”, she told AFP.
This aerial photo taken on August 26, 2026, shows a general view with the Kinabatangan River and surrounding jungle in Sukau, a small village near Sandakan in Sabah state on the island of Borneo. — AFP pic
In a recent incident, a herd of 20 elephants stomped into palm oil smallholdings and three villages, terrifying residents.
No one was injured, but the incident prompted calls for stronger deterrents, including upgraded electric fencing.
“People don’t feel safe around elephants, and that’s when conflict happens,” Farina said.
The animosity worsens when the animals, especially adventurous bulls, which can weigh up to five tonnes, cleverly bypass electric fencing to feast on palm trees or saplings.
That is why Farina and her team of 17 conservationists prioritise coexistence.
A herd of wild Bornean elephants crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
“We’re working to increase people’s tolerance, to increase connectivity space for elephants and to find a long-term solution,” she said.
Based in Sukau, a hamlet on the crocodile-infested banks of the Kinabatangan river, Seratu Aatai runs an outreach programme in plantation schools, distributes information pamphlets and has designated “community wildlife guardians” who help usher away elephants that have wandered into human habitation.
“Before, we didn’t know how to manage living near them,” said homestay owner Firah Kazenn, 21, who recently encountered elephants behind her home in Sukau.
“The elephants were unmonitored, and many were lost to conflict. Now, with the Seratu Aatai unit, they are protected, and the community is actively involved too,” Firah told AFP.
This photo taken on August 27, 2026, shows boats docked along the shore of the Kinabatangan River and surrounded with jungle in Sukau. — AFP pic
“We’ve learnt safe ways to guide the elephants away when they come too close to our homes, without harming them,” she added.
‘Win-win situation’
Farina believes the best way to protect the animals is by creating “elephant corridors” — pathways through plantations connecting patches of habitat.
She is hoping to convince seven plantations in the area that elephants are “an ecological reality, rather than an occasional disturbance”.
But it will be a challenge.
Fierce competition driven by tight, volatile margins means many producers are not keen to sacrifice land for corridors, said Muhammad Al Shafieq bin Mustafa, a former plantation manager in Sukau and now a palm oil industry specialist.
Members of the team led by Farina measuring the length of a female Bornean elephant during a GPS collaring operation as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
“Those plantations that do commit and are willing to work with people like Farina often do not get the recognition that they deserve or the financial support that they need, especially from Western palm oil buyers,” he told AFP.
Industry-funded conservation associations say plantations have made progress in becoming sustainable palm oil producers but face difficult economic realities.
“It needs to be a win-win situation between the planters and also the wildlife,” said Daniel Pamin, conservation and sustainability executive at the Malaysian Palm Oil Green Conservation Foundation.
This photo taken on August 24, 2026, shows Nabila Sarkawi, a veterinary officer with the Sabah Wildlife Department at Sepilok (back), watching Khairun Amlan (right) administering a multivitamin injection during a GPS collaring operation led by Farina (unseen) as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. — AFP pic
Farina believes change will come.
Before, locals used the Malay word “halau”, meaning “chase away” or “banish”, when talking about elephants.
“Now, we are working to get people to say... ‘walking’ or ‘escorting’ out the elephant.” — AFP
A wild male Bornean elephant crossing the Kinabatangan River with a plastic bag wrapped around its trunk in Sukau. — AFP pic

Title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks, stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Malaysia has condemned in the strongest terms the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and expressed solidarity with the Kingdom.
Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the security and safety of its population, in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law.
“Malaysia also supports all efforts towards de-escalation and an immediate end to the hostilities,” it said in a statement on Monday.
The statement comes amid an escalation in hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, with Saudi authorities saying a ballistic missile fired towards Riyadh on September 19 was intercepted and destroyed.
Saudi Gazette
reported that the Houthis also attempted to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in Baish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu, but the attacks were thwarted.
Saudi Press Agency reported that on September 14, Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif injured 13 civilians and damaged several houses and vehicles, according to the Saudi-led coalition.
The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.
“Malaysia attaches great importance to its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia, and remains fully committed to further strengthening this partnership for mutual interests of both nations,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Five-year-old girl found dead after uncle allegedly throws her into river in Johor
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 21 — A five-year-old girl was found dead, believed to have been thrown into a river by her uncle in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, this morning.
Kota Tinggi District Police Chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9:30am regarding a 37-year-old local man who went on a rampage armed with a machete while chasing a 40-year-old man.
He said initial investigations found that prior to the incident, the suspect was believed to have thrown the victim into the river.
“Acting on information, a police team went to the location of the incident, and a struggle ensued resulting in injuries to one of the personnel, but the suspect was eventually arrested,” he said in a statement today.
Yusof said a medical assistant confirmed the death, and the victim’s body was sent to Kota Tinggi Hospital before being brought to the Forensic Department of Pasir Gudang Hospital tomorrow for a post-mortem.
He added that the motive and cause of the incident are still under investigation, and the suspect is also believed to have mental health issues.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Anwar leaves Istana Negeri Sembilan after hour-long audience with Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held a nearly hour-long audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, this evening, as a dispute over the status of the state executive council continued to unfold.
Anwar left Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here after completing the audience, Astro Awani reported.
He had arrived at the palace grounds at about 6pm.
No details of the discussions during the meeting were immediately disclosed.
The audience came after Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members with immediate effect late last night.
According to a statement by Istana Negeri Sembilan comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali, the decision was made after the ruler found that the exco members had breached their oaths of office.
The palace cited Article 38(5) of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959, which states that a member of the State Executive Council holds office for as long as he or she has the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The exco members had taken their oaths and signed pledges of loyalty on August 7 before being appointed to the council.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, however, disputed the validity of their removal in a statement today.
He said any action to dismiss or terminate the membership of an exco member without the advice or formal request of the Menteri Besar was “invalid, unconstitutional and had no legal effect”.
Ismail said he had not been consulted or provided advice on the removal of any exco member under Article 38(5).
He maintained there was therefore no need to submit a new list of proposed exco members, saying the existing line-up remained legally valid and would continue to carry out its duties as usual.
